item.title: Why Europe’s decarbonisation is failing
item.description: Fossil-fuel companies have built a network of lobbying organisations that top the list of meetings with the EU Commission

item.title: The animal cruelty the EU-Mercosur deal will be importing to Europe
item.description: Without meaningful safeguards, the EU-Mercosur agreement – as it stands – risks locking the EU into a system that expands imports of meat produced under conditions that fall far below EU regulations. The deal would lower tariffs — without requiring imported products to meet equivalent European animal welfare standards.

item.title: Lithuania sounds alarm over possible arms-smuggling balloons from Belarus
item.description: Lithuania has warned that balloons used to smuggle cigarettes from Belarus could soon be repurposed to transport weapons, as Vilnius considers deploying anti-personnel mines along their shared border. Some of the balloons hover at 10km altitudes with speeds up to 200km.

item.title: EU sets out plans to double aid for Greenland amid Trump threats
item.description: The EU will double its funding for Greenland and hopes to ramp up cooperation with Nuuk and other overseas countries and territories, the bloc’s international partnerships commissioner told MEPs on Wednesday, after weeks of heightened tensions and the threat of US military action to seize the island.

item.title: Artists and songwriters need updated EU copyright law for AI, parliament committee says
item.description: A European Parliament legal committee approved on Wednesday a report on copyright protections and AI — calling for updated laws, transparency in AI training, and artist compensation.

item.title: Next EU budget will see member states pay 48 percent more, auditors find
item.description: The European Court of Auditors estimates that despite more instruments to increase 'own resources' revenues, member states contributions to the next 2028-2034 EU budget will increase by 48 percent.

item.title: EU defends measures to close ‘loopholes’ in carbon border tax
item.description: The EU defends temporary carbon border tax exemption for fertilisers for farmers — while tightening the levy on steel and aluminium-heavy products.

item.title: Threat of ‘tactical’ Russian nuclear strike in Europe growing, think-tank warns
item.description: The risk of a small Russian nuclear strike in Europe is rising as the US military deterrent wanes, a British think-tank has warned.

item.title: How the Kremlin turns schoolchildren into future soldiers in occupied Ukraine
item.description: When Russian forces occupy a Ukrainian town, schools are often targeted first. An investigation into hundreds of Telegram posts from Russian propaganda channels operating in occupied Ukraine since 2022 reveals a systematic campaign to militarise and indoctrinate children through schools.

item.title: Fear, power politics and migration: whatever happened to Germany’s ‘welcome culture’?
item.description: Ten years ago, Germany symbolised Europe’s 'Willkommenskultur' (Welcome Culture). Chancellor Angela Merkel’s decision to open borders to refugees in 2015 was framed as a moral and historical responsibility. What has happened since?
